feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Tokyo and Osaka, Japan recorded their latest-ever 30 °C days on 21 October
entry.summary: Tokyo and Osaka both passed 30 °C on 21 October, the latest date in the year either city has reached that mark. — Sources: The Star / Japan Meteorological Agency data, 21 October 2026

entry.title: Hong Kong issued its latest-ever Very Hot Weather Warning on 21 October
entry.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory issued a Very Hot Weather Warning at 6:45 am on 21 October, its latest in any year, with about 33 °C in urban areas. — Sources: Hong Kong Observatory via The Standard and Dimsum Daily, 21 October 2026 · South China Morning Post, 23 October 2026

entry.title: Beitbridge, Zimbabwe reached 44 °C on 20 October
entry.summary: Zimbabwe's Meteorological Services Department recorded 44 °C at Beitbridge on 20 October, with 41 °C at Gwanda, Binga, Kariba and Buffalo Range. — Sources: Zimbabwe Meteorological Services Department via MyZimbabwe, 22 October 2026 · Namibia Meteorological Service via The Namibian, 21 October 2026

entry.title: Malawi upgraded its heatwave warning to severe and moved school activities out of midday
entry.summary: Malawi's weather service upgraded its southern heatwave warning to severe on 20 October and widened it to central areas, with highs up to 42 °C. — Sources: Malawi Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services, warnings of 18 and 20 October 2026 · Malawi24, 21 October 2026

entry.title: Lima, Peru set an October high as Peru's weather service warns of a hot summer
entry.summary: Carabayllo in Lima reached 30 °C on 18 October, a new October high for the city. — Sources: Senamhi via Infobae, 18 and 21 October 2026

entry.title: Australia's northern heatwave peaked at 44.8 °C and its last warnings were cancelled
entry.summary: Western Australia's hottest reading in the 17 to 21 October heatwave was 44.8 °C at Mandora on 19 October, well short of the state record of 50.7 °C. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology station observations and warnings, 17 to 24 October 2026

entry.title: England's reservoir storage held at 54 percent, with 13 reservoirs exceptionally low
entry.summary: The Environment Agency's report for 16 to 22 October keeps six regions of England in severe drought and national reservoir storage at 54 percent, about 22 percent below average. — Sources: Environment Agency, Dry weather and drought in England, 16 to 22 October 2026, published 23 October

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany rose to 29 centimetres before falling back
entry.summary: Germany's federal gauge at Kaub read 10 centimetres at 6 am on 17 to 19 October, rose to 29 centimetres on 23 October after rain, and read 23 centimetres on 24 October. — Sources: Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration, Pegelonline Kaub gauge, 17 to 24 October 2026 · wetter.net, 19 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: Severn Trent's 49.8 percent reservoir figure and drought permit date from 2025
entry.summary: The 49.8 percent figure and the drought permit for the River Derwent published here on 22 and 23 October both date from October 2025. — Sources: Severn Trent Water, raw water storage levels, 19 October 2026 · Severn Trent Water, Ambergate drought permit 2025

entry.title: Singapore's haze returned to unhealthy in every region on 24 October
entry.summary: All five regions read unhealthy at noon on 24 October, from 116 in the south to 152 in the west. — Sources: National Environment Agency, hourly 24-hour PSI data, 1 to 24 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire-hotspot count reached 31,893 on 23 October, the highest this week
entry.summary: Indonesia's daily hotspot count rose from 8,973 on 20 October to 18,985 on 22 October and 31,893 on 23 October, of which 2,011 were high-confidence detections. Central Kalimantan accounted for 19,703. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry hotspot data via Katadata, 20 to 23 October 2026

entry.title: Malaysia's haze worsened again, with 21 areas unhealthy on 24 October
entry.summary: Malaysia recorded unhealthy air in 21 areas at 9 am on 24 October. Larkin in Johor and Seremban were highest at an air pollutant index of 169, with six more Johor areas in the unhealthy band. — Sources: Bernama, 24 October 2026

entry.title: Santa Ana winds drove fires in southern California, including the 570-acre Norte Fire
entry.summary: The Norte Fire in south Orange County, California started on 16 October during a Santa Ana wind event and damaged homes before full containment at 570 acres on 23 October. — Sources: IQAir wildfire map, 23 October 2026

entry.title: Mexico recorded 156 heat deaths in its 2026 season, nearly double 2025
entry.summary: Mexico's health ministry closed the March to October heat season with 156 deaths, 150 from heat stroke, against 83 in 2025. — Sources: Mexico Ministry of Health weekly heat surveillance, reported 20 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's haze-season respiratory infections passed 280,000, more than 40,000 in young children
entry.summary: Indonesia has recorded more than 280,000 acute respiratory infections since 18 August, more than 40,000 of them in young children. — Sources: The Rakyat Post, 20 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: the US occupational heat-death estimate is a preprint with a central figure of 9,800 a year
entry.summary: The University of Michigan study shown here on 18 October is an unreviewed preprint. — Sources: Shkembi, Schinasi, Payne-Sturges and Neitzel, medRxiv preprint, 30 January 2026

entry.title: The UK workplace temperature bill's second reading is now listed for 19 March 2027
entry.summary: The Maximum Workplace Temperature Bill would set up a body to recommend a maximum safe workplace temperature. — Sources: UK Parliament Bills API, bill 4263 stages, updated 22 October 2026

entry.title: The European Commission aims to adopt the Quality Jobs Act on 3 December
entry.summary: EU employment ministers agreed on 19 October that the Quality Jobs Act should cover the impact of climate-related risks at work. The Commission aims to adopt it on 3 December. — Sources: Agence Europe, 20 October 2026 · Irish Presidency of the Council, EPSCO main results, 19 October 2026

entry.title: The Philippine labour department is drafting rules to suspend work in extreme heat
entry.summary: The Philippine labour department said on 21 October it is drafting guidelines, with the state weather service, on when heat should suspend work in the CALABARZON region. — Sources: Daily Tribune, 21 October 2026
